newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted easier on Friday in sympathy with the benchmark treasury bill rate which came down at Thursday's weekly auction, dealers said.
"The market is still very liquid and rates have softened in line with the treasury bill rate which came down yesterday (Thursday)," one dealer commented.

Dealers said market activity was still unaffected by the on-going strike action by civil servants demanding salary increments from president Robert Mugabe's government but added that monetary losses incurred through the action could affect the market at a later stage.
On Friday, discount houses were buying treasury bills from the central Reserve Bank at 22.66 percent, down from the previous week's 23.12 percent but were selling them unchanged at 22.5 percent.

NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 23.75 and 23 percent respectively from 24 and 23 percent while bankers acceptances were at 23 and 22.75 from 23.5 and 22.75 percent.
Call money was however quoted firmer at 22.5 percent from 22 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the market surplus, prompted by treasury bill maturities the previous day, at Z$409 million up from Z$183 million.
